questions.title: On a still-open charge, is half the capture the refund or just the limit?
questions.question: When a merchant refunds a charge that hasn't settled yet, do we always send back half the capture, or do we send back what the merchant typed, up to half the capture? For example, on a $50 charge where the merchant asks for $10, do we refund $10 or $25?

options.label: Limit: refund what the merchant typed, up to half the capture
options.clarification: While a charge is still open, the card is credited the amount the merchant typed, but never more than half of the captured amount (rounded down to the cent).

options.label: Fixed: always refund half the capture
options.clarification: While a charge is still open, the card is credited exactly half of the captured amount (rounded down to the cent), whatever amount the merchant typed.

questions.title: Does a same-day refund on a settled charge follow the still-open rule?
questions.question: If a charge has already settled but the merchant asks for a refund within 24 hours of capture, is it handled like a still-open charge (half the capture) or like a normal settled refund (the amount typed, up to the full capture)? For example, a $50 charge settled 12 hours ago where the merchant asks for $35: refund $35 or $25?

options.label: Settled rule: once settled, it's a normal refund, even the same day
options.clarification: Whether a charge is still open is decided only by whether it has settled; a settled charge always gets the written refund (the amount typed, up to the full capture), even within 24 hours of capture.

options.label: Still-open rule: any request within 24 hours of capture
options.clarification: A refund requested less than 24 hours after capture follows the still-open rule even if the charge has already settled; the written settled-refund policy applies only to settled charges at least 24 hours old.
